LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NBA Betting Sites Legal Betting States Sports Betting Guide DFS millionaire Mike McClure shares his top daily Fantasy picks and advice for Houston vs. Indianapolis on 'Thursday Night Football' Imagn Images NFL Week 11 kicks off with an NFC South battle on 'Thursday Night Football' as the Indianapolis Colts visit the Houston Texans (-12.5, 44.5) at 8:15 p.m. ET. The large spread indicates that NFL DFS lineups may heavily lean towards Texans like C.J. Stroud, Nico Collins and Dalton Schultz. But Jonathan Taylor and Tyler Warren remain some of the best at their positions for Indy and will surely be sought after for TNF DFS lineups. Both teams, however, have questions regarding specific position groups in Houston's injury-ravaged running backs and Indy's trade-gutted wide receivers. Houston running back Woody Marks (concussion) and Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) have been ruled out, though David Montgomery (groin) has been cleared to return. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. Taylor carried the ball 13 times for 46 yards in Week 9 against Dallas and 16 times for 83 yards in Week 10 against Miami. He had 23 carries and cleared this prop in Week 3 against Houston, which is 20th in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.0 yards per carry this season. The Colts star has at least 50 rushing yards in seven of his 10 games this season, picking up at least 45 rushing yards in nine of his games. Taylor is still the safest bet to go off for an Indy team that moved on from both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. The clear No. 1 option for this Houston offense through the air, Collins has already seen 55 targets from C.J. Stroud, reeling in 37 of them for 478 yards. He was targeted 16 times in the loss to Cleveland in Week 10, and with the Houston running game struggling in 2026, I expect the offense to rely on Stroud throwing the ball on Thursday. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. After missing all of last season and the start of the 2026 season recovering from a brutal knee injury, Tank Dell is back – and thriving – with Stroud at quarterback. Dell and Stroud have some great chemistry in their time together in the NFL, and the young receiver has played just under 50 percent of the offensive snaps in back-to-back weeks. In Week 9, Dell had four grabs for 105 yards and a score, receiving nine targets from Stroud. He then followed that up with a three-catch game (on four targets) against Cleveland. Dell isn’t going to lead this receiver room in snaps, but he’s getting looks from Stroud when he’s out there and is now facing a defense that is 18th in EPA/Pass, allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the league. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. The prop market projects Watson to threw for 207.5 passing yards while he's -273 to throw a touchdown and -123 to throw an interception. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. home.headline: Colts rule out 5 players for Week 11 Thursday Night Football game vs. Houston Texans
home.blurb: Colts rule out 5 players for Week 11 Thursday Night Football game vs. Houston Texans Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts on Wednesday ruled out five players for Thursday night against the Texans. The Colts on Wednesday ruled out tight end Will Mallory (hamstring), tackle Bernhard Raimann (concussion), defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf), tackle Jalen Travis (knee) and cornerback Charvarius Ward Sr. (knee) for Thursday night's game against the Houston Texans. Cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf), wide receiver Anthony Gould (toe), tackle Charlie Heck (personal) and long snapper Luke Rhodes (hamstring) are all listed as questionable. Gardner left Sunday's game with his injury and did not return. Rhodes missed Sunday's game and was listed as a nonparticipant in Monday's practice if it had taken place, but was a limited participant Tuesday and Wednesday. news Colts rule out 6 ahead of Week 10 vs. Dolphins Head coach Shane Steichen ruled the players out Friday. news Colts rule out CB Justin Walley, LB Akeem Davis-Gaither for Week 9 news Colts rule out WR Anthony Gould, CB Justin Walley for Week 8 against Jaguars news Colts rule out TE Tyler Warren, WR Anthony Gould, CB Sauce Gardner for Week 7 news Colts rule out LB Jaylon Carlies, WR Ashton Dulin ahead for Week 6 news Colts rule out WR Ashton Dulin, DE Arden Key and LB Jaylon Carlies for Week 5 news Colts do not rule out any players ahead of Week 4 game against Washington Commanders news Colts rule out wide receiver Ashton Dulin for Week 3 game vs. Houston Texans news Colts rule out WR Ashton Dulin for Week 2 game against Kansas City Chiefs news Colts do not rule out any players for Week 1 game against Baltimore Ravens news Colts rule out CB Sauce Gardner, TE Will Mallory for Week 18 game vs. Houston Texans Abby Halpin Contributing Writer This will be the second straight game missed for Tillery. Raimann and Ward both left Sunday's game due to their respective injuries. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies (neck) was placed on IR Tuesday and will miss at least the next four games. Head coach Shane Steichen made the announcement Friday. Neither player has practiced this week due to injury. Ashton Dulin (ankle) will miss his second straight game. Gardner left the Colts' Week 17 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with a calf injury. Inside Football With Rick Venturi COPYRIGHT © 2026 COLTS, INC.

Since its inception in 1987 on "The Tracy Ullman Show", the nation's longest-running cartoon series and sitcom has become a cultural force with its satirical look at society and culture today. More importantly, it showed Americans that television cartoons can be relished by adults. So I'm hoping you'll catch my meaning when I use a famous Simpsons quote to personify the Buffalo Bills . The NFL team that famously lost four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s is enjoying a Milhouse moment right now. Milhouse Van Houten is Bart Simpson's lovably awkward and loyal best friend. To co-opt a famous Simpsons quote, "everything's comin' up Milhouse" for the 8-1 Bills, who own the best record in the AFC halfway through the regular season. With the hapless Jets in the rearview mirror and the awful Dolphins coming to town, it's a great time for Bills fans to enjoy the AFC's best record at the season's halfway point. Will it stay that way for the NFL's most cursed franchise? Who knows. The early predictions for the Bills vs. Dolphins matchup this week are decidedly in Buffalo's favor. So, maybe this Milhouse moment is sticking around. Bills vs. Dolphins odds (Odds as of Monday afternoon) The Bills are 16.5-point favorites. The over/under is 45.5 points. The money line for the Bills is -1400 (bet $1,400 to win $100) and the Raiders are +950 (bet $100 to win $950). On paper, this is the most one-sided matchup of the season in the NFL, and with the game being played at Highmark Stadium, it's highly unlikely that the Bills will stub their toe. "After this game, Buffalo has a tremendously difficult five-game stretch that will probably determine whether they can grab the AFC's No. 1 seed for the first time since 1993. AZCentral.com: Bills 31, Dolphins 14 Jeremy Cluff writes: "The Bills opened as a massive 16.5-point favorite against the Dolphins. Will Buffalo win a sixth straight game? Yes, it will. Bookies.Com: Take the under Bill Speros writes: "The Bills (8-1 SU and 7-2 ATS) tore up the Jets 31-12 in Week 10 and are off to the franchise's best start in 35 years. The Bills' combo of Josh Allen and James Cook bludgeons opposing defenses. The 1-8 Dolphins are a surprising 5-4 ATS, and this is the largest NFL spread of the season so far. Our model has Buffalo winning by 15.0, 1.5 points shy of the 16.5-point line, and projects a 46.4-point total against the 47.5 line. Miami scores 16.4 points per game and has been held under 25 in eight of nine games. This week, the Bills keep the ball on the ground and the Dolphins off the field." Miami, 1-8 this season, faces a tough battle against the Bills, who are 8-1 this year and currently in position to claim the top spot in the AFC playoff picture. Miami will also be starting quarterback Kyle McCord for just the second time in his career as he continues to fill in for the injured Malik Willis. The injury concerns do not end there, however, as Miami has seen three defensive tackles, Zach Sieler, Zeek Biggers, and Jordan Phillips, land on the injured reserve over the past week. On the first injury report of the week, the Dolphins were without center Aaron Brewer (concussion), punter Bradley Pinion (right groin), cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad), continuing the injury issues the team is currently battling through. As the preparations for the Bills game continue, the Dolphins are also supporting the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, perhaps the most anticipated video game ever. Scheduled to release today, GTA VI is set in a fictionalized version of Miami called Vice City and features a local football team, the Manatees, whose primary colors are aqua and pink. While the Dolphins have not broken out a "Vice City" jersey combination like the Miami Heat have, they are still partnering with Rockstar Games, the game's developers, to ensure the game is represented in Hard Rock Stadium. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Miami Dolphins (1-8) head to Highmark Stadium on Sunday looking to crawl out of the cellar in the AFC East. Their opponent, the Buffalo Bills (8-1) will be looking to maintain their hold on not only the top spot in the division, but in all the AFC. The Bills have won five in a row and are off to their best start since 1991 while the Dolphins are in full tear down so we can rebuild mode. The contrast is especially sharp offensively: Buffalo leads the NFL at 31.9 points per game and averages 399.7 yards, while Miami ranks 31st at 16.4 points per game. Miami enters after a frustrating 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts, but rookie Kyle McCord provided one of the few encouraging developments in what has been a difficult season to say the least. Making his first NFL start, McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards without an interception and added a three-yard rushing touchdown as the Dolphins rallied from a 21-7 third-quarter deficit. Miami also scored on a 59-yard Chris Johnson interception return and got 76 rushing yards from Ollie Gordon II , but McCord’s fumble near his own goal line was recovered for an Indianapolis touchdown. The kicking game also proved costly as Zane Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point in a two-point defeat. Buffalo, meanwhile, continued its surge with a 31-12 road victory over the New York Jets, turning a relatively close 10-6 halftime lead into a convincing win. Josh Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception, but again did major damage with his legs, scoring twice on one-yard runs before hitting DJ Moore for a 45-yard touchdown in the third quarter. James Cook III supplied the knockout punch, finishing with 157 yards on 18 carries and breaking a 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. Buffalo’s defense kept the Jets out of the end zone entirely, and the Bills have allowed just 28 total points over their last three games. The rivalry itself provides Miami with at least some reason for optimism, even though Buffalo has controlled it for much of the Josh Allen era. The Bills have won four of the last five meetings, but the Dolphins snapped a lengthy skid in emphatic fashion the last time these teams played, beating Buffalo 30-13 in Miami on Nov. 9, 2025. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

The Bills ruled out Benford early in the fourth quarter due to a groin injury. Although there's a possibility Benford can play Sunday depending upon the severity, groin issues usually take more than one week to heal. While the Bills will presumably hold their top cornerback out of practice this week, there's still a chance he will be active on game day, much like right tackle Spencer Brown in Week 10 . As for Alford, he is in the league-mandated concussion protocol after twice being evaluated for a head injury during the 31-12 win over the Jets. He must now pass through the five-stage process before being permitted to return to action. It's not a matchup many Saints supporters are excited about seeing. The Bears are an NFC title contender, while the Saints have repeatedly squandered opportunities to take over the NFC South from the Carolina Panthers (4-5). Still, there are reasons for optimism that go in the Saints' favor. Mike Moraitis of Chicago Bears on Si noted what the Bears will need to watch out for against the Saints this weekend. Per Moraitis, the Saints' wide receiver corps could put the greatest strain on the Bears defense. Here's some of what Moraitis had to say about New Orleans' three top receivers. "The Saints already had a solid one-two punch at wide receiver in Chris Olave and the ascending Devaugh Vele, but New Orleans added rookie Jordyn Tyson into the mix a few weeks ago. Tyson was on the shelf for the first seven games because of a hamstring injury. After a quiet game in his NFL debut, Tyson emerged in Week 10 with 11 catches for 80 yards. Tyson has played the majority of his snaps in the slot, where the Bears have an injury concern this week with Kyler Gordon, who is dealing with a shoulder injury that has him labeled as day-to-day. But, as we noted, Tyson isn't the only one the Bears need to be worried about. Both Vele and Olave are in the midst of career-best seasons and can cause major head aches for a Bears secondary that has seen struggles, and namely with Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson. Luckily for Chicago, rookie Malik Muhammad has been better than expected in his first season and has provided some stability on the outside." While some will write off his impact, we still have only got one game with Travis Etienne Jr. cleared for play at running back since his injury. His effect may take time to be felt, but we could see the beginnings of it this week against the Bears. Add in what the receiver corps is able to do after Tyson's 11-catch breakout game against the Panthers last weekend, and New Orleans could finally start to generate the offense we hoped to see when Tyson was drafted. The Saints haven't been far off from playing playoff caliber football, but the frustration has been mounting as we wait for it to finally happen. New Orleans will get its shot against the Bears.

away.blurb: Just one New Orleans Saints player was upgraded to full practice reps on this week's second injury report, and it wasn't Jordyn Tyson. Veteran running back Alvin Kamara (not injury related) practiced fully on Thursday after the team gave him a rest day to start the week. Everyone else saw the same level of participation as they did on Wednesday. For the first time in weeks, all four running backs on the 53-man roster practiced fully with CJ Donaldson (shoulder) cleared to return. Here's a recap. Tyson (chest), the rookie wide receiver, was limited along with backup corner Decamerion Richardson. Six others did not participate at all: starting cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) on defense, plus multiple starters on the offensive line like center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), and Asim Richards (knee), who had been filling in for Fuaga. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) missed practice due to a personal matter, which we now know to be his release from the team. It'll take a few days to work out the financial details as he looks for a way to join a contender. away.blurb: The Chicago Bears will likely be absent one of their top defenders against the New Orleans Saints coming off the bye week, as nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon's shoulder has kept him out of practice two straight days. The nickel cornerback has been excellent since he returned from a soft-tissue concern that held him out of the first five games of the year. However, the injury-prone Gordon played in just four contests before finding himself hurt again and it's now a real threat that he will miss the Bears' return to action against the Saints at Soldier Field. Harrison Graham of "Bears Now" pointed out on Wednesday that Gordon's shoulder injury is less problematic than his chronic soft-tissue injuries, even if he does miss a game or two moving forward. Muscle strains cost Gordon all but three contests in 2025. "Jeffery Simmons says he's good to go despite a knee ailment: ‘I got 99 problems but this ain't one. New Orleans Saints Praised in Chicago Bears Game Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Orleans Saints Praised in Chicago Bears Game Preview Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 4:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints (3-6) take on the Chicago Bears on Sunday. It's not a matchup many Saints supporters are excited about seeing. The Bears are an NFC title contender, while the Saints have repeatedly squandered opportunities to take over the NFC South from the Carolina Panthers (4-5). Still, there are reasons for optimism that go in the Saints' favor. Here's some of what Moraitis had to say about New Orleans' three top receivers. "The Saints already had a solid one-two punch at wide receiver in Chris Olave and the ascending Devaugh Vele, but New Orleans added rookie Jordyn Tyson into the mix a few weeks ago. Tyson was on the shelf for the first seven games because of a hamstring injury. After a quiet game in his NFL debut, Tyson emerged in Week 10 with 11 catches for 80 yards. Tyson has played the majority of his snaps in the slot, where the Bears have an injury concern this week with Kyler Gordon, who is dealing with a shoulder injury that has him labeled as day-to-day. But, as we noted, Tyson isn't the only one the Bears need to be worried about. Both Vele and Olave are in the midst of career-best seasons and can cause major head aches for a Bears secondary that has seen struggles, and namely with Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson. Luckily for Chicago, rookie Malik Muhammad has been better than expected in his first season and has provided some stability on the outside." While some will write off his impact, we still have only got one game with Travis Etienne Jr. cleared for play at running back since his injury. His effect may take time to be felt, but we could see the beginnings of it this week against the Bears. Add in what the receiver corps is able to do after Tyson's 11-catch breakout game against the Panthers last weekend, and New Orleans could finally start to generate the offense we hoped to see when Tyson was drafted. The Saints haven't been far off from playing playoff caliber football, but the frustration has been mounting as we wait for it to finally happen. New Orleans will get its shot against the Bears.

home.headline: Jordyn Tyson still limited on updated Saints injury report vs. Bears
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Just one New Orleans Saints player was upgraded to full practice reps on this week's second injury report, and it wasn't Jordyn Tyson. Veteran running back Alvin Kamara (not injury related) practiced fully on Thursday after the team gave him a rest day to start the week. Everyone else saw the same level of participation as they did on Wednesday. For the first time in weeks, all four running backs on the 53-man roster practiced fully with CJ Donaldson (shoulder) cleared to return. Here's a recap. Tyson (chest), the rookie wide receiver, was limited along with backup corner Decamerion Richardson. Six others did not participate at all: starting cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) on defense, plus multiple starters on the offensive line like center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), and Asim Richards (knee), who had been filling in for Fuaga. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) missed practice due to a personal matter, which we now know to be his release from the team. It'll take a few days to work out the financial details as he looks for a way to join a contender. The Bears did not actually practice Wednesday, though it had sessions on Monday and Tuesday and will again on Thursday and Friday coming out of a bye week. Still, NFL rules mandate each team submit an injury estimation for players on off days between Wednesdays-Fridays of game weeks, which led the Bears to list Simmons with a practice participation projection of "limited" based on the knee issue. According to Pro Football Network's player impact scores, which take into account both traditional and advanced metrics, the 29 year old is the best DT in football again in 2026 out of 119 players who have seen enough snaps to qualify through Week 11 with a perfect score of 100.0 . That actually ties him with Quinnen Williams who plays for the Dallas Cowboys, of all defenses. Gordon has been excellent for the Bears since returning after missing the first five games of the season due to a soft-tissue injury. He suffered a shoulder issue against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers a couple of weeks back and was a DNP [did not practice] on Wednesday's report. The Chicago Bears made a Super Bowl bet on Jeffery Simmons that might just pay off if he can stay health, which made the news of the All-Pro defensive tackle's appearance on the injury report Wednesday all the more unsettling around the Windy City. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen on Thursday sent a blunt message on Simmons' status following the waves his designation made across the media, the team's fanbase and social media in general. "I don't anticipate any issues with him," Allen said of Simmons , per Courtney Cronin of ESPN. Chicago hosts the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field in Week 11. Jeffery Simmons Has Changed All 3 Levels of Bears' Defense in Just 2 Games Getty Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons of the Chicago Bears. Simmons was the best defensive tackle in the NFL last season based on his status as a first-team All-Pro. In two games since joining the Bears, Simmons has tallied 10 combined tackles, including three tackles for loss, two sacks and two pass breakups. He has also elevated the play of his teammates along the defensive line, who see less overall attention and easier matchups because of Simmons' presence. Meanwhile, members of Chicago's secondary have already raved about how much easier their jobs are because of the pressure Simmons puts on opposing quarterbacks and how offenses adjust their approach before even taking snaps so as to account for the elite presence Simmons creates in the middle of the Bears' defense. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. As Saleh himself said after the team's latest loss, you aren't going to win allowing 40 points a game. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Tennessee Titans (1-8) travel to AT&T Stadium on Sunday afternoon for a matchup with the Dallas Cowboys (4-6). This is a must win for Dallas should they hope to stay within reach of the first-place Giants in the NFC East while Tennessee is looking to see continued growth from their young quarterback, Cam Ward . Each team takes the field looking to snap a losing streak. The Titans have dropped three straight and sit last in the AFC South, while Dallas is in second place in the NFC East and as noted, needs a win this weekend to remain in the postseason conversation. Tennessee has had issues scoring touchdowns (18.6 points/game), but this is not expected to be a low-scoring affair. Dallas ranks sixth in scoring at 28.6 points per game, but the Cowboys are allowing 28.2 points and a league-worst 406.3 yards per game. The Titans’ defense is nearly as generous, allowing 405.6 yards per game. Tennessee’s latest loss was a 40-23 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars, dropping the Titans to 1-8 despite periods of competitive football. The Titans trailed only 16-10 at halftime and stayed within 23-16 entering the fourth quarter before Jacksonville finally pulled away. Tennessee totaled 342 yards but converted only 18 percent of its third downs, while its defense surrendered 459 yards, 26 first downs and 40 points. Cam Ward threw touchdown passes to Daniel Bellinger and Tony Pollard , with the latter going for 32 yards to pull Tennessee within 30-23 midway through the fourth, while Joey Slye connected on field goals of 54, 53 and 50 yards. But Trevor Lawrence carved up the Titans for 352 yards and three touchdowns, and Jacksonville scored the final 10 points to put the game away. Dallas is coming off an even wilder game, a 46-40 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The game was not as close as the final score. The 49ers accumulated 584 total yards, the most Dallas has ever allowed in a home game, averaged 9.4 yards per play and produced three touchdowns of at least 66 yards. Christian McCaffrey alone amassed 223 scrimmage yards and three scores as Dallas’ late comeback fell short. Dak Prescott completed 58.8 percent of his throws for 343 yards and five touchdowns, matching his career high for touchdown passes, and George Pickens erupted for 11 catches, 145 yards and three scores. CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy each caught touchdowns as Dallas piled up 439 yards, but the Cowboys simply couldn’t stop San Francisco. The central storyline Sunday is whether Tennessee can take advantage of a Dallas defense that has been dominated nearly every week this season. The Cowboys are allowing a league-worst 154.1 rushing yards per game, potentially creating an avenue for Tennessee to protect Ward, lean on its backfield and keep Prescott off the field. These teams have alternated wins in each of their last five meetings: Dallas won 27-13 in 2022, Tennessee won 28-14 at AT&T Stadium in 2018, the Cowboys won 26-10 in 2014, the Titans won 34-27 in 2010 and Dallas won 45-14 in 2006. home.headline: What’s Up With the Cowboys’ Injuries? Tough Report Released Wednesday
home.blurb: Seven Dallas Cowboys players did not practice Wednesday, including starters Tyler Booker, DaRon Bland and Jake Ferguson, four days before the 1-8 Tennessee Titans arrive at AT&T Stadium. The DNP list consisted of tight end Ferguson (knee and ankle), cornerback Bland (ankle), right guard Booker (ankle), outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle), safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle). Outside linebacker Von Miller also sat out, but the report lists his absence as a veteran rest day, not an injury. No game designations have been issued — yet. Booker, a 2025 first-round pick, had started every game at right guard with an 84.8 Pro Football Focus grade . Sprains like his typically sideline players four to six weeks , according to NFL Network, though Booker could return within four. T.J. Bass steps in at right guard. Bland's sprain is in the opposite ankle from the one that limited him in practice last week. Cobie Durant took over most outside cornerback work after he left. Placing either on injured reserve would cost four games, and Dallas has used most of its eight return designations this season. So who plays? Ferguson is not expected to play against Tennessee , and Booker and Bland are expected to miss multiple weeks. Miller, listed for rest only, is expected to be available, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle and foot) practiced fully. Locke, Ezeiruaku and Mingo remain uncertain until Friday's report. Cowboys Defenders Speak Out on DC Christian Parker's Demotion What’s Up With the Cowboys’ Injuries? Tough Report Released Wednesday Unlock the latest Heavy on Cowboys news — direct to your inbox. The Dallas Cowboys are struggling this season. That's no secret with a 4-6 record after Week 10. Things got so bad that in what one commentator called a “downright bizarre decision,” the Cowboys suddenly demoted defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Wednesday. But there may be another factor just as important in the Cowboys' struggles, one made clear by a team announcement on Wednesday — injuries. The absences land on a defense that already surrenders 28.2 points per game , leaving open how much cushion a last-place opponent really provides. Booker, Bland Injuries Reshape Cowboys Lineup Booker and Bland both suffered high ankle sprains in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Bland went down on San Francisco's first touchdown drive while tackling Deebo Samuel Sr., and Booker followed later in the first half. Neither returned. That left the 4-6 Cowboys reshuffling on both sides of the ball. “The two big ones I think will be [guard Tyler] Book[er] with the ankle and [cornerback DaRon] Bland with the ankle,” head coach Brian Schottenheimer said, as quoted by EssentiallySports . “Both those guys could miss a little bit of time,” Schottenheimer said Monday, as quoted by Dallas Sports Journal . Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 11 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+215) vs. Detroit Lions It didn’t go well for me last week betting against the Lions. But this time it will be different! Remember, a broken clock is right twice a day. Anyway, Detroit will have a few challenges in this one, including facing a tough Tampa Bay defense a week after having to play a game in Germany. The Lions’ explosive offense had trouble generating points against Green Bay, Minnesota, and Miami (the Dolphins!) before bouncing back against the Patriots last week. Perhaps Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles could use some of those blueprints to slow down star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Also, this will be the Lions’ first game without star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who sustained a season-ending knee injury against the Patriots. Peter Dewey Week 11 Upset Pick Baltimore Ravens (+114) vs. Carolina Panthers If you’re going to make a case for an upset this week where there are five teams favored by double digits, I don’t mind targeting the Baltimore Ravens in their clash with the Carolina Panthers. Carolina barely came away with a win over a bad New Orleans team in Week 10, and it remains pretty banged up on both sides of the ball. The Panthers are a top-10 team in the league in EPA/Play on offense, but they’re in the middle of the pack in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball. Carolina is also allowing 4.4 yards per carry on the ground, so this could be the week Derrick Henry gets going. The Ravens are coming off a pretty huge loss at home against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night, but Jacoby Brissett wasn’t bad in that matchup, and he may have led this Baltimore team to a win had Zay Flowers not lost a costly fumble late in the fourth quarter. I don’t think that any team in the NFC South should be trusted as a favorite, as the division as a whole is just 4-17 against the AFC North over the last four seasons and 63-111 overall against non-NFC South teams during that stretch. Iain MacMillan Week 11 Upset Pick The Lions' already bad and injured defense continues to take big hits. Now it's their star pass-rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the season after celebrating a sack against the Patriots on Sunday. He joins a list that includes D.J. Reed, Kerby Joseph, Devin White, and Jack Campbell, who are on the injured list. It's enough to convince me that now is the time to sell your Lions' stock. Detroit now has to take on a Buccaneers team that's fresh off a BYE week, and that ranks in the top five in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. While the Lions' offense is certainly elite, they're going to struggle to rack up the amount of points they need to aid their limping defense. Baker Mayfield's injury status is up in the air, which could make this bet tough to win, but if he plays, we're in a great spot. Even if he doesn't, Tampa Bay can win this game with their defense and rushing attack alone. They're my upset pick of the week. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Erik Schlitt · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers will square off in a Week 11 NFC showdown. Lions coach Dan Campbell and Bucs coach Todd Bowles have a long history together—dating back to when Campbell played in Dallas (2005)—and they've gone head-to-head four times in the last three seasons, with Detroit winning three of those matchups. "Tampa Bay Bucs, competitive, physical unit. Known (Buccaneers Head Coach) Todd Bowles a long time. Obviously have got a ton of respect for him and what he's about. And this defense is playing outstanding football. And offensively, they're committed to the run game, time of possession. They're trying to force you into making errors. And really, the last three games, they played some pretty good football." Let's take a closer look at the Bucs' coaching staff, the scheme that they run, and some scouting notes from previously viewed games. Bucs head coach: Todd Bowles NFL coaching seasons: 27 seasons (Bucs, Jets, Cardinals, Eagles, Dolphins, Cowboys, Browns) Head coaching seasons: 10 seasons (Dolphins 2011—interim, Jets 2015-18, Bucs 2022-present) Defensive coordinator seasons : 6 seasons (Eagles 2012, Cardinals 2013-14, Bucs 2019-2021) Influences: Bill Parcells, Mike Zimmer, Mike Nolan, Chuck Pagano, Paul Pasqualoni, Juan Castillo Coached under : Parcells, Bruce Arians, Andy Reid, Tony Soarano, Wade Phillips, Butch Davis, Al Groh Playcaller : Yes (Defense) Offensive coordinator: Zac Robinson NFL coaching seasons : 8 seasons (Bucs, Falcons, Rams) QB seasons in NFL : 4 years (Bengals, Lions, Seahawks, Patriots) Offensive coordinator seasons : 3 seasons (Bucs 2026, Falcons 2024-25) Previous coaching seasons : Passing game coordinator, QB coach, Assistant QB coach, Asst. WR coach Influences: Sean McVay, Bill O'Brien & Tom Brady (Pats), Kyle Shanahan Coached under : McVay, Kevin Stefanski Offensive scheme Passing game : McVay West Coast Running scheme : Shanahan outside zone and gap schemes Staples of scheme : Very similar scheme to what the Bucs have had with Baker Mayfield at QB Robinson comes from the same McVay/Shanahan tree as other former Bucs' OCs, Dave Canales (Panthers HC), Liam Coen (Jaguars HC), and Josh Grizzard (Eagles PGC) Mainly 11 Personnel: 63.3% of the time 12-personnel: 24%, 13-personnel: 8.5%, 21-personnel: 4% More shotgun (53%) than under center (37%), which is a change from previous regimes Staples: Play-action (27.5%, 8th most), pre-snap motion, and bunch formations are staples Balanced approach, pure progression reads, rhythm passing plays Want to attack and push the ball vertically QB (Mayfield, not UDFA Jalon Daniels) has the freedom at the line to check into better plays It's been an up-and-down season for Mayfield, who played in Weeks 1-3, missed Weeks 4-6 with a thumb (throwing hand) injury, returned for Weeks 7-9, and is now injured again (foot) and may not play in this game When Mayfield has played, his numbers have regressed; passer rating of 74.9 (31st in the NFL) In his six games played, he has less than 1,000 total passing yards Mayfield has more interceptions than touchdowns thrown: just 3 TDs and 4 INTs Mayfield has also fumbled six times Bottom three in the NFL in: passing yards, pass yards per play, explosive passing plays, passing success rate Offensive line has done well to mitigate pressures: 107 over nine games (8th fewest) But they've allowed 27 sacks (24th) and a 10.1% sack rate (30th) Mayfield 18 sacks over 6 games; Daniels 9 sacks over 3 games Introduced more balanced zone run concepts; a change from last year's inside zone/downhill approach Outside zone: 22.8%; inside zone: 17.2%; gap/man: 25%; Counters: 18.7% Run game has been very successful No. 1 in the NFL in average rushing yards per game: 163.9; rush yards per play: 5.0; and explosive runs over the last four games: 16.1% Success rate over last four games: 47.4% (5th) EPA per rush: -0.02 (10th) Essentially, they're wearing teams down with consistent success and hitting on big plays in the run game Dan Campbell on the Bucs' offense : "Offensively we'll see what happens with (QB) Baker (Mayfield), but obviously have got a lot of respect for him, what he's capable of, what he's done in this league. Good receivers on the perimeter. Obviously (WR Chris) Godwin (Jr.) and (WR Emeka) Egbuka over there and they got speed with (WR Tez Johnson) 15. (TE Cade) Otton's a solid tight end and this O-line is just an all-day sucker. They'll just keep coming all day long." Campbell on the Bucs' rushing attack : "Bucky (Irving)'s a hell of a back. Honestly, I should have started with him. I mean, this guy is, he really is their lifeblood for what they do offensively in this run game. And this O-line will lean on you, and they're all-day suckers, man. I mean, they will bring it all day long. And he has just got that; he's got a feel. He's got a feel for finding that crease. He understands he's got spatial awareness. He knows when these defenders are closing in on him, he can backdoor it, he can dip under, he can burst back out. And then once you get him into the second level of the defense, he's even more dangerous. So, they want to get him going here. And (RB Kenneth) Gainwell, we know too. I think Gainwell's a damn good back too. Very versatile. So, there's no secret there." Run Game Coordinator/OLB: Larry Foote For three seasons (2022-24), Foote (a Michigan native) served as the Bucs' co-defensive coordinator alongside current Lions defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers, while Bowles maintained play-calling duties. In 2025, the Bucs shifted titles, naming Foote Run Game Coordinator and outside linebackers coach. NFL coaching seasons: 12 seasons (Bucs, Cardinals) LB seasons in NFL : 13 seasons (Cardinals, Steelers, Lions) Roles with Bucs : OLB coach, Co-DC/Passing game coordinator/ILB coach, Run game coordinator/OLB coach Influences: Bruce Arians, Todd Bowles, Dick LeBeau, Jim Schwartz Coached under: Arians, Bowles, Steve Wilks Defensive scheme Base : Attacking 3-4 Coverage : Zone, single-high Staples of scheme : Aggressive, attacking scheme: 2-gapping DL and stand-up pass-rushing OLBs Nickel formations: 67% of the time means a lot of 2-4-5 formations Blitz-heavy: 43.9% (2nd most in the NFL, behind only the Vikings) Utilize blitz to rush the passer and stop the run Very creative blitzer scheme—although there's a lot of tape on Bowles' style/tendencies 3-3 Fire zones, replacement blitzing, Phantom blitzing DL stunts and slants designed to disrupt up front Pressures have declined: 112 through nine games (23rd); pressure rate: 33% (24th) As has sack production: 17 sacks (24th); sack rate: 5% (25th) Zone-heavy (85%), specifically Cover-3: 52% of the time Cover-2: 9%, Cover-4: 24%, Cover-6: 2.5% When in man coverage, it's mainly Cover-1: 9.5%, with some Cover-0 (2.5%) mixed in Bump-and-run coverage approach with corners to stay tight early in route Done well to eliminate explosive passing plays: less than 5% of attempts (No. 1 in the NFL) Done well to slow down explosive run plays: 8% (8th) Fewest rushing yards allowed per game: 79.1 (1st) Rushing yards per play: 3.5 (3rd) EPA per rush: -0.13 (3rd) Success rate over last four games: 41.2% (16th) Dan Campbell on the Bucs' defense: "They've got some impact players, guys that make it very difficult for you. Obviously (NT) Vita Vea there in the middle and (LB) Alex (Anzalone) is playing at a high level. (LB Josiah) Trotter, (S Antoine) Winfield (Jr.). I mean, we can keep going here. (DL Calijah) Kancey and they have got a ton of guys on defense playing really good football." Campbell on the Bucs' rookies making an impact: "Trotter's the best example of that. Every week he gets better and better and better in this case. The key and diagnose and his running, he's downhill and I mean he sees it and he is all out, man. I mean this guy is aggressive. So, he's really growing and he's just the best example of that, but their young guys are growing."

away.headline: Unexpected Baker Mayfield injury update gives Buccaneers a boost ahead of Lions matchup
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers began preparing for their pivotal Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions under the assumption that they’d be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield. Mayfield was in a walking boot after suffering a foot strain in Week 9, and his status was up in the air after missing practice on Wednesday . NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport didn’t close the door on Mayfield playing, but he did report that it was trending towards rookie backup Jalon Daniels getting the start this week. But in a surprising turn of events, Mayfield returned to practice on Thursday and is now gearing up to play on Sunday. Baker Mayfield is suddenly trending toward playing against Lions in Week 11 Despite all initial signs indicating otherwise , Mayfield is now expected to get the start against the Lions. The Buccaneers quarterback told reporters that he feels ready, and that if he continues on this path, he’ll play on Sunday. However, he also added that if he isn’t ready and feels Jalon Daniels would give the team a better chance to win, he’ll have no shame taking a backseat and letting the rookie start in his place. “I’m doing everything I can to get all the treatment and rehab possible and you know, prepare like a professional… If I continue that I imagine being able to play… if I feel like J.D. gives us a better option to win, no shame admitting that. So, we’ll see how it goes but progressing well.” Nobody can question Mayfield’s toughness as he looks to power through yet another injury, and even though he’s struggled this season, there’s no doubt he gives the team the best chance to win, even if he isn’t at 100%. Daniels undeniably has a lot of potential, but he went 1-2 as a starter, both losses featured multiple backbreaking turnovers from the rookie. Going into a hostile environment in Detroit against a red-hot 7-2 Lions team, having the veteran franchise quarterback at the helm rather than an undrafted rookie makes a big difference. If the Buccaneers can pull off the road upset, their odds of winning the NFC South would increase significantly. If Mayfield plays, there can be no excuses. Tampa Bay needs him to start looking like the quarterback that they handed a three-year, $165 million contract extension during the offseason. If there was ever a time for Mayfield and the Buccaneers’ 32nd-ranked passing offense to get back on track, it’s against the Lions and their bottom-five pass defense. The Buccaneers need their franchise quarterback to deliver when it matters most, and Sunday’s matchup against Detroit gives Mayfield a golden opportunity to change the narrative surrounding this season. Aside from Mayfield, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) was the only other Buccaneer held out of practice Wednesday. home.blurb: Mayfield said he practiced in a "limited fashion." The thumb injury held him out of action for three games. After Mayfield returned, he led the Buccaneers to two crucial divisional victories over the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons — although the team didn't need him to complete a single pass in the latter contest. Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is "trending toward" playing on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, NFL insider James Palmer reported Thursday. Mayfield suffered a foot sprain during Tampa Bay's 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. He's still dealing with pain from the injury but is "pushing through it," according to Palmer. Mayfield told reporters that he "felt good" during a press conference on Thursday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . "Just trying to get as much as I can in," Mayfield said about his practice. "The mental side of it. Hopefully, [I can] get more tomorrow and go from there." When asked if he felt like he could play this week, Mayfield nodded and confirmed: "I'm ready." The 31-year-old signed a three-year, $165 million contract extension this offseason, but the early production has left a lot to be desired. Mayfield opened the 2026 season with three consecutive losses before dislocating his thumb during a 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3. The Buccaneers went into their Week 10 bye with a 3-6 record, but they can still win a division title in the NFC South despite their struggles. Although they currently trail the Panthers by one game, ESPN Analytics gives the Buccaneers a 61 percent chance of winning the division this season. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Chiefs-Cardinals betting line & prediction: Kansas City’s biggest mismatch yet? Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) runs drills during Chiefs practice on Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Dominick Williams/dowilliams@kcstar.com) Pete Sweeney · Kansas City Star Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs won their second game in a row Sunday when they overpowered the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 , improving to 7-2 on the NFL season. The Arizona Cardinals lost their second straight 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams to drop to 3-7. Here's what to know about their matchup on Sunday ... How to watch Cardinals at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -15.5 Behind the ARI-KC matchup While the Chiefs were getting back on track by taking care of business against the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons over the past two weeks, the Cardinals have been falling apart at the seams. Sunday's monumental mismatch starts at the quarterback position, where rookie Carson Beck is expected to make his second career start after completing just 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions against the Rams. Arizona has turned to Beck after trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and watching last year's Chiefs backup Gardner Minshew tear the UCL in his throwing arm. Understanding the reality of the situation, linebacker Drue Tranquill showed the two-time national champion with Georgia some respect before outlining the problems he may face against a Chiefs defense that has come alive with eight sacks over the last two games. "He's obviously got winning pedigree — he did it in college," Tranquill said of Beck. "He'll get another start under his belt this week in a great environment, so it's a good opportunity for him, but we'll have to execute our pre-snap looks, have to execute our game plan in terms of owning our leverage, taking away options he might want to go to early in the down. And then hopefully, as the game progresses, we can get the pass rush going, get them in known passing situations and get them on the ground." With running back Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, on injured reserve, the Cardinals' best path to an upset is extending possessions with veteran back Tyler Allgeier and utilizing first-team All-Pro tight end Trey McBride. McBride has managed 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns despite Arizona's struggles. With wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Michael Wilson (neck) out for the remainder of the season, that's left McBride as Beck's lone viable option. Among Arizona's available players, tight end Elijah Higgins ranks second on the team in receiving yards with 18 catches for 162 yards. "They've got some good tight ends, and so we'll have to be on it," Tranquill said. "They're big, they're physical, can make contested catches. And so we'll have to own our leverage and be physical at the top of the stem and not allow them to create separation, and try to get the ball off these guys." Arizona's protection has allowed 28 sacks this season — tied for the sixth-most in the league. Meanwhile, Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis enters Sunday with at least one sack in each of his last three games , Ashton Gillotte is in the midst of a two-game sack streak and Chris Jones has registered 2.5 sacks over the last two games. The Cardinals' offensive line is a point to watch, as they played against the Rams without starting center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), who had already replaced left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps tear). Both Froholdt and Williams were limited in practice Wednesday. The situation doesn't get any easier for the Cardinals on the other side of the ball. In the run game, the Cardinals allow 4.2 yards per carry, and through the air, they give up 8.2 yards per pass attempt. The Chiefs opted to rest Kenneth Walker last Sunday against the Falcons because of groin tightness, and he didn't practice Wednesday . That means rookie Emmett Johnson could make his second straight start after compiling 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off his best passing stat line of the season, in which he threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Falcons. But bigger than that were the chunk gains, as the outing included seven completions of 20 yards or more. While the Cardinals' secondary is susceptible to explosive passing plays, if there is one area of concern for the Chiefs, it's that they're more than capable of generating pressure. Led by safety Budda Baker with 3.5 sacks and outside linebackers Zaven Collins and Josh Sweat with three apiece, the Cardinals have registered 21 sacks this season. "They do a great job of causing havoc and causing pressure, and they do a great job throughout a lot of these football games of kind of stopping the offenses," Mahomes said. "There's been parts where offenses have kind of found the big plays, and it has to come within rhythm. It's not like you can kind of hunt those things. You have to get the ball out of your hand, because if you don't, they'll get home, and they'll cause negative plays." Protection will be imperative for what could be a shorthanded Chiefs offensive line. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) both missed practice Wednesday, and it remains to be seen whether newly signed veteran Fred Johnson can provide a boost after joining Kansas City's practice squad Tuesday. In his opening game in a Kansas City uniform , wide receiver Josh Downs turned 11 snaps into four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown. Wide receiver Rashee Rice led the Chiefs with 82 yards, and Downs, Andrew Armstrong and rookie Cyrus Allen all reached the end zone. Sunday's game will give way to a short Thanksgiving week for the Chiefs, with perhaps their most important game of the season awaiting them Thursday night against the Buffalo Bills. Given the grand disparity between the two clubs, look for head coach Andy Reid to be mindful about how long he plays some of his key contributors, especially those dealing with injuries. Cardinals-Chiefs game prediction In my 13 years analyzing and previewing Chiefs games, I'm not sure that I can recall a matchup this lopsided going in. But as they say, that's why they play the games. Winner: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 9 | Cover: Chiefs Sweeney's record: (7-2-0) | Against the spread: (5-4-0)

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Arizona Cardinals (3-7) travel to Arrowhead Stadium to take on the Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) on Sunday for a matchup between teams heading in completely opposite directions. The Cards are floundering, battling an inordinate number of injuries at the skill positions, and now starting rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes has the Chiefs in first in the AFC West and just one game behind Buffalo for the top spot in the AFC (Spoiler Alert: the Bills and Chiefs play on Thanksgiving on NBC/Peacock.) It should come as no surprise that the statistical gap is significant: the Cardinals average just 18.4 points per game while allowing 28.9, whereas Kansas City scores 26.3 per game and owns one of the league’s stingiest defenses at 17.3 points allowed per game…and KC is undefeated at home this season (4-0). The Cardinals are coming off an ugly 34-6 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, a game in which their offense essentially disappeared after the opening quarter. Two 49-yard field goals from Chad Ryland gave Arizona a 6-3 lead, but those would be its only points. Beck, making his first NFL start, completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards with two interceptions, while the Cardinals managed only 142 total yards, 34 rushing yards and six first downs. They went 0-for-6 on third down and held the ball for just 17:37. Trey McBride led the team with five catches for 37 yards. The Chiefs delivered a performance that was basically the exact opposite of that put forth by the Cards. KC rolled past the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 for their second straight win. Mahomes was sensational, completing 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns without throwing an interception. Rookie Emmett Johnson carried the ball 22 times for 101 yards and also caught a touchdown pass, helping Kansas City pile up 461 yards of total offense. The Kansas City defense forced two turnovers and held Atlanta to one touchdown in five red-zone trips. These teams do not meet often, but the recent regular-season history decidedly favors Kansas City. The Chiefs have won the last two meetings, including a 44-21 victory at Arizona in the 2022 season opener, when Mahomes threw five touchdown passes, and a 26-14 win at Arrowhead Stadium in 2018; the Cardinals’ last regular-season victory in the series was 17-14 in 2014.
