away.blurb: Heading into Sunday's game, the Rams will have three players listed as questionable: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl. Garrett isn't practicing on Friday, as Sean McVay said the Rams are just "being smart" with him. McVay expects Garrett to play, saying that he's "feeling good" and building on a strong performance last week. McDuffie and Curl will be limited in practice, and the Rams will see how they feel before determining their statuses for Sunday's game. McDuffie has missed three of the last four games but McVay said earlier in the week that he's "optimistic" about a return on Sunday. Curl didn't practice at all last week due to a foot injury and still managed to play against the Commanders. Finally, Terrance Ferguson and Steve Avila have both been ruled out, which isn't surprising. They're both expected to miss multiple weeks with their hamstring injuries. Update: The Rams and Cardinals released their full injury reports. In addition to McDuffie, Garrett and Curl, Davis Allen and Joe Cardona are both questionable. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid's injury update after Week 10's win over Falcons spells bad news for 2024 NFL Draft pick
home.blurb: Kiffin's return to Tennessee Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya. Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. Pittsburgh is coming off an embarrassing primetime defeat to the Cincinnati Bengals, losing 38-18 in a game that wasn't nearly as close as the score indicates. The Steelers managed only 40 yards of offense in the first half and lost possession of first place in the AFC North. The Eagles are in a free fall, losing seven games in a row. Only the winless Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) have a worse losing streak. They're coming off their bye week after a 19-11 home loss to the New York Giants on November 8. Both teams are looking for positivity and momentum following a terrible week for the Steelers and an unimaginably poor season for the Eagles in 2026. The Steelers are 4.5-point road favorites on FanDuel Sportsbook entering Week 11. The Steelers are -200 on the moneyline for the 1 p.m. game on Sunday. Pittsburgh is 6-3 on the season, but 2-3 away from home. Mike McCarthy's team is averaging 17.4 points per game in those matches. The over/under total is set at 38.5 points. Philly has historically dominated the matchup at home, but is without former Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts. Philadelphia has won the last 11 games played on the eastern side of the state. Pittsburgh defeated the Eagles 38-29 at Heinz Field on October 11, 2020. The Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965. Their last victory came before the Super Bowl era, the Penguins were founded, the Pirates won their last two World Series titles, and NFL and AFL merged. Pittsburgh needs a win to keep pace with the Bengals and hold off the Cleveland Browns, who are making a charge in the AFC Wild Card race. The Steelers look to prevent a snowball effect after a crushing Cincinnati loss that could be the turning point of the 2026 season. ​ Let us know what you think in the comments . Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) head to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. Smith’s availability is especially significant because the Eagles badly need another proven weapon alongside Saquon Barkley to make life easier for Milton against a Pittsburgh defense featuring T.J. Watt and one of the NFL’s better pass rushes. Beyond Pittsburgh’s attempt to rebound and Philadelphia’s effort to stop its seven-game skid, the matchup carries a fascinating piece of Pennsylvania rivalry history. The Eagles lead the all-time series 50-29-3, and Pittsburgh has endured an extraordinary drought in Philadelphia. The Steelers have not won in Philly since 1965. They have lost their last 11 games against the Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love. Philadelphia has also dominated the two most recent meetings, winning 27-13 in Philadelphia on Dec. 15, 2024, after a 35-13 home victory in 2022; Pittsburgh’s last win in the series was a 38-29 victory at Heinz Field in 2020. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.blurb: We could get that answer over the next few weeks, starting with a trip to eastern Pennsylvania. The Steelers haven’t won in Philly in over six decades. This would be an ideal time to break that trend and pick up a big bounce-back win over their in-state rival. Nothing brings out the yinzers and the brotherly love like Pittsburgh vs. Philadelphia. Herbig is the biggest concern on the Steelers’ injury report heading into Sunday. The outside linebacker hasn’t practiced this week because of hip and rib injuries, and he was the only player listed as DNP on Thursday. Queen practiced on a limited basis both days with a new hand injury, so his status is worth watching as Friday’s game designations get closer. The rest of the report is mostly good news for Pittsburgh. Elliott was limited Wednesday with the knee injury he picked up in pregame warmups Sunday, then practiced fully Thursday. Pittman went from limited to full participation, and Wilson and Dunker were full participants both days. away.blurb: Taking a look at Wednesday's Week 11 injury report, the Steelers listed safety DeShon Elliott practice as a limited participant with his newly acquired knee injury. Injury updates are flying left and right, and the Pittsburgh Steelers just received some news on the status of one of their standout safeties who picked up a surprise setback just hours before last week's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals . Elliott, who began his NFL career with the Baltimore Ravens , also played for the Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins before joining the Steelers in 2024. He signed a two-year, $12.5 million extension with the Steelers following his stellar 2024 season, but his success was derailed in year two after he suffered a season-ending hyperextended knee and hamstring tear midway through the 2025 season. We at Steelers Wire wish Elliott a speedy recovery, as he's one of the league's best tackling safeties when healthy. away.headline: FINAL Chargers vs Ravens Injury Reports: Updates on Njoku, McConkey, Stanley
away.blurb: MLB Probable Pitchers & Starting Lineups MLB Odds Public Betting Props Probable Pitchers & Lineups Weather Reports ATS Records Futures News The 0-8 Chargers battle the 4-5 Ravens to close out Week 10 on Monday Night Football Find out the injury statuses of several players for this AFC tilt on MNF The LAC injury report includes ten players, with massive uncertainty surrounding their pass-catchers. Meanwhile, the BAL injury report contains just three names, but a key questionable tag on the O-line remains a focal point. I will break down how these confirmed absences sway the point spread, totals, and prop markets before kickoff. Tracking NFL public betting splits is useful, but exploiting injury inefficiencies is where the sharp edge lives. With McConkey out and Brenen Thompson doubtful, Quentin Johnston (13 receptions, 260 yards) and Tre' Harris (21 receptions, 262 yards) will absorb the vast majority of outside boundary routes. They will be tasked with exploiting a Baltimore defensive backfield that has surrendered 241.9 passing yards per game and 15 passing touchdowns through nine contests. At tight end, David Njoku carries a questionable tag with a fibula injury, complicating a game with a low 39-point total. Njoku logged full practice participation, suggesting strong availability. The Chargers are also navigating major pocket presence concerns heading into this matchup. Branson Taylor is out, while Trey Pipkins III and Kayode Awosika are both questionable on the offensive line. Protection breakdowns have plagued the Chargers all autumn, with Los Angeles surrendering 31 sacks for 227 lost yards through eight games (3.9 sacks allowed per contest). The Ravens currently sit as a 4.5-point home favorite at a discounted -111 price, accompanied by a heavy -227 moneyline. Their injury list is notably short. Rookie running back Adam Randall has been on IR all season. Randall is questionable with a neck issue, though his full participation implies he should suit up. Tackle Ronnie Stanley is also questionable, strictly designated for rest. Stanley's projected presence on the blind side is vital for newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who steps in after season-ending injuries to both Lamar Jackson (thumb surgery) and Tyler Huntley (turf toe). The only confirmed absence for the Ravens is safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who is out with a knee injury. Hawkins being sidelined places an even greater coverage and box responsibility onto All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton and cornerback Marlon Humphrey. home.blurb: Kiffin's return to Tennessee Last week, we talked about the good news of Mike Jackson and Jonathon Brooks fully practicing. It turns out they only took scout team reps and should have been listed as limited participants. Both ended up out for the game against the Saints this past Sunday. Now they are both full participants again, but this time it's for real. Mike Jackson has already said he expects to play this Sunday, which is a huge add for a defense that seems to be turning the corner with new defensive coordinator Todd Wash. He might be joined by rookie Will Lee, who was starting to show flashes before he suffered his own muscle injury. That dup would obviously be a gargantuan upgrade over what the Panthers have had on the outside the last few weeks. No offense. Nnamdi Madubuike – DNP – Hamstring The Ravens' injury report does a disservice to their actual injury woes. Lamar Jackson has had a nightmare season in terms of injuries. He's on injured reserve, and so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. The Ravens acquired Jacoby Brissett in an act of desperation, but that hasn't panned out so far. They're relying on newly acquired Cam Jurgens to center the offensive line after they lost several centers to injury over the first few weeks of the season. It turns out he just might not be any good anymore. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 16, 2026 at 4:54 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their fifth straight game and eighth of their last nine on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it's possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. It's tough to win games like that, but the Jets may prove to be an elixir for what ails the Chargers. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think the Chargers will beat the Jets next Sunday. It's come to this: the Jets aren't even favored over a winless team. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 40.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +156 while the Chargers are -186. A loss next Sunday against the Chargers would be just another humiliation for the Jets. Perhaps they can find a way to avoid that fate after being beaten by a winless Dolphins team earlier this season. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Does it really matter in another lost Jets season? J-E-T-S! No, not at the top of the standings...but at the bottom. Both teams are far removed from playoff consideration to the point where this game is all about the 2027 NFL Entry Draft. The first overall pick is at stake. New York has lost five straight, while Los Angeles finally snapped an 11-game losing streak dating to last season with its first victory of 2026 this past Monday night. The Jets have been the more productive offense statistically, averaging 19.4 points and 341.9 yards per game, compared with a Chargers’ attack sitting last in the league at 16.0 points per game. Still, Los Angeles enters Sunday with a little momentum and actually favored to win. The Jets’ latest setback was a 31-12 home loss to Buffalo, a game that was competitive at halftime before unraveling after the break. New York trailed just 10-6 at intermission and ultimately produced 376 yards, but the offense failed to score a touchdown for the second consecutive game, with Jason Sanders accounting for all 12 points on four field goals. Geno Smith completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards but briefly exited for a concussion evaluation before returning and then suffering an ankle injury in the third quarter. Rookie Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut in relief, completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception, while Garrett Wilson caught seven passes for 106 yards and Breece Hall finished with more than 100 yards from scrimmage. Los Angeles, meanwhile, finally found their way into the win column Monday night with a 23-20 road victory over Baltimore, and the formula looked exactly like what Jim Harbaugh wants from his team. The Chargers dominated the line of scrimmage, outrushing Baltimore 160-16. Omarion Hampton led the way with 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. Justin Herbert threw for only 129 yards but played turnover-free football for the first time this season. He added 51 rushing yards, including a 22-yard touchdown on Los Angeles’ opening possession. Cameron Dicker kicked four field goals, and the defense essentially erased Derrick Henry , limiting him to 10 yards on 10 carries despite his two short-yardage touchdowns. Sunday’s central questions are whether the Chargers’ defense can outmuscle the Jets along the line as they did against the Ravens and if the Jets can turn long drives into touchdowns which has been a challenge for them consistently all season. The New York Jets could turn to rookie Cade Klubnik for his first NFL start Sunday, with Geno Smith’s ankle injury leaving coach Aaron Glenn without a firm answer at quarterback. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Glenn said. The decision concerns Smith’s health, not an announced benching. Glenn said Monday that Smith would retain the job if healthy, The Associated Press reported . Tests did not reveal a serious ankle injury, but New York still needs to determine whether he can play. The Jets are 2-8 after five consecutive losses. They have not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, and a change at quarterback would put a fourth-round pick from Clemson in charge of an offense struggling to finish drives. Klubnik made his professional debut against Buffalo and completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception. He also ran three times for 26 yards. Glenn praised the rookie’s mobility Wednesday and said he would continue getting practice opportunities against the first- and second-team defenses. Klubnik had little time to settle in, but his first possession produced a 10-play, 61-yard drive and a field goal. Two scrambles moved the chains on that series, the team reported Monday . He played 37 snaps in relief of Smith. Running back Breece Hall came away encouraged by how Klubnik handled the huddle. Hall said the rookie showed more than he expected while stepping into a game without the preparation afforded a starter. “Just seeing how he came in, that was a huge growth step for him,” Hall said. away.headline: Geno Smith: 'The Plan' Is to Let This Week Unfold, Then Return as Jets' Starter at LA
away.blurb: It starts with the quarterback's attitude regarding some injuries, -- "just normal football stuff," that he experienced against Buffalo. He's on the Jets' injury report, listed as limited for Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury, but he foresees having the ball back in his hands so he can operate the offense against the Chargers on Sunday. "It's football. It comes with it," he said of the play, which wasn't flagged by the officials. "If they throw a flag, they do, it they don't, they don't. My job is to go out there and play and not worry about it." "My job is to be coachable and be the player, and I respect Coach Glenn and everything that he says," Smith said. "He makes the calls, so I'll do as I've always done. When I was a backup for years, I prepared as if I was the starter, and nothing changes for me. ... I do appreciate Coach going out and saying that. He doesn't have to say that, but I do appreciate it." home.headline: Geno Smith Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Jets QB's Status Ahead of Chargers Game
home.blurb: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith will participate in Wednesday's practice in limited capacity after suffering multiple injuries in last Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters. The Jets (2-8) are on track for a high pick in the 2027 NFL draft. Should Smith remain available to start, the Jets may not get a longer look at Klubnik before deciding whether to use that pick on a quarterback. Smith left Sunday's game twice for a concussion evaluation and then for the ankle injury. He will be listed on the injury report with an ankle injury, Glenn said. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday Smith "underwent tests today that did not reveal anything major." "Smith, whose ankle provided the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week," Rapoport reported. The Jets are preparing to play Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers. Glenn confirmed earlier this week Smith will continue starting over Cade Klubnik if healthy. When asked Wednesday if he expected Smith to play against the Chargers, Glenn said , "We'll see how the week goes." Smith left Sunday's game in a golf cart, then visited the X-rays before leaving without visible crutches or walking boot, per ESPN's Rich Cimini . ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Smith "was in pain Sunday but showed signs of improvement Monday, giving confidence that he will try to push through and play Sunday vs. Los Angeles." SNYs Connor Hughes reported the Jets shut down offers at the trade deadline for Smith, who has completed 67.1 percent of his passes with 2,226 passing yards to go along with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions in 10 games of his age-36 season. Klubnik saw his first action of the season when he went 11-for-20 with 137 yards after replacing Smith in Sunday's third quarter. He scrambled for another 26 yards while throwing no touchdowns and an interception. ▶️ Full Bills-Jets Recap 05:23 Glenn said Monday he felt it would be "disrespectful" to Smith to consider starting Klubnik in order to conduct more evaluation of the rookie quarterback down the stretch. Bo Nix and the Broncos (7-2) look to win and keep pace with the Chiefs atop the AFC West. Las Vegas has lost two straight while Denver has reeled off five straight wins. This will be Mendoza’s first start on the road, and it comes against one of the more ferocious and stingy defenses in the NFL. Denver’s defense is allowing only 20.7 points per game. Their pass rush has produced 26 sacks, with Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen at 4.5 apiece. Last week the Raiders surrendered six sacks. Speaking of last week, Las Vegas is coming off a 21-13 home loss to the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, a game in which Mendoza showed promise early in his first NFL start before the Raiders’ offense faded. He completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards in the first half and scored on a 10-yard run but finished just 17-of-29 for 143 yards as Seattle’s pressure took over and sacked him six times. Even more damaging was the loss of star tight end Brock Bowers , who injured his ankle and played only 11 snaps. His status is questionable for this weekend and is certainly worth monitoring. Denver, meanwhile, is back after sitting out last week on their bye. Their fifth consecutive win thanks to a 26-21 road victory over the Carolina Panthers back on November 8. Quarterback Bo Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns, connecting with Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant for scores, while rookie running back Jonah Coleman rushed 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown. That balanced performance was encouraging for a team that ranks only 30th in the NFL in total yardage at 277.3 yards per game. away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 7:13 PM . away.headline: Raiders dealt considerable injury disadvantage with Broncos coming off their bye
away.blurb: After a physical game against the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, the Raiders are dealing with a few bumps and bruises; nothing out of the ordinary. But the Broncos are coming off their bye, so they practically have a clean bill of health heading into this heated divisional matchup. Concussions can often keep a player out for one game, but because Denver had its bye week, both players were able to make a full recovery. And that's a good thing, because head and neck health is important, but it certainly does not help Las Vegas' chances of winning in Week 11. Matt Gay being a bit banged up is not great, either. He has been lights-out as a kicker this year, and with the ball moving differently at a mile above sea level on Sunday, Las Vegas needs him to be at the top of his game. Hip injuries can be worrisome for a kicker, depending on the hip, of course. With the Broncos not having any injury concerns this week, fresh off their bye, it hurts to have Bowers potentially out and another starter at least banged up. But the Raiders haven't done well playing against injured teams this year, so maybe they'll thrive with the shoe on the other foot. Not even close to everything has gone right for the Las Vegas Raiders during the 2026 NFL season. But one benefit that they've carried in their back pocket throughout the campaign has been relatively good health , which has given them an edge in seemingly every single game. Have the Silver and Black always taken advantage of that edge? No. But in several contests, they have gotten to face skeleton crews with a fully staffed roster. That is changing this week, though, with the AFC West rival Denver Broncos on the schedule for Week 11. All year, Las Vegas has been at an advantage in the injury department. Now, they're up against it. Broncos' injury report is as thin as it gets before clash with Raiders Both teams released their injury reports after Wednesday's practice. Here is how things went in Denver: Nobody is wishing injury on the Broncos, but of course, as fate would have it, they get a handful of key players back when they face the Raiders. Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss, both of whom suffered concussions in Week 9, are back at practice with no limitations and will play on Sunday. Talanoa Hufanga is also back this week, it seems, after missing four straight games for the Broncos' secondary. He was playing well before suffering an ankle injury, and he missed an entire month. But with an extra week off to prepare, he will re-emerge against the Raiders, of course. Caleb Loehner is also back this week after beginning the season on IR. He is a promising young tight end prospect that, if you can believe anything that Sean Payton says, has a bright future in Denver. The Broncos have been looking for a spark at tight end, so he could be involved right away. Vegas is 4-6 overall and 0-1 since trading away week one starter Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. Cousins won in his Vikings return this past Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Las Vegas Raiders aim to see a rejuvenated Fernando Mendoza following his rough NFL debut. But he may need to roll without All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Bowers is dealing with ankle and quad injuries still. He didn’t participate in Wednesday practice according to the injury report . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Yet Bowers isn’t the only TE who landed on the injury report. Backup Ian Thomas is dealing with a calf ailment. Bowers played through pain against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, catching just two passes for 18 yards. Mendoza, again, received a rough welcome into the NFL. Seattle sacked him six times and bottled Mendoza to 143 yards . The Seahawks even sent star cornerback Devon Witherspoon on two blitzes, eventually leading to a team-high two sacks. Witherspoon even nailed Mendoza on a disguised overload blitz look that instead saw Seattle drop four defenders into coverage, but got Witherspoon busting freely down the middle. So the Raiders could see a thinner TE room. Michael Mayer is one healthy option the Silver and Black can turn to against Denver. away.headline: Broncos get boost regarding injuries days before facing Raiders
away.blurb: Coming out of their Week 10 bye, every player on the 53-man roster was present at Wednesday’s practice, including several key contributors who have been dealing with injuries. Related Articles NFL Calls Out NBC’s Mike Florio for On-Air Joke About Mike Vrabel The Denver Broncos could be getting some massive reinforcements at just the right time. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, cornerbacks Riley Moss and Kris Abrams-Draine, and safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones were all back on the field as Denver prepares for its AFC West showdown with the visiting Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Waddle and Moss are the biggest developments as both suffered concussions during Denver’s Week 9 win over the Carolina Panthers. Neither player finished that game, leaving the Broncos without two important pieces on opposite sides of the ball. Getting Waddle back would give quarterback Bo Nix another explosive receiving threat and Moss would help restore Denver’s starting cornerback pairing alongside Patrick Surtain II. Hufanga could also provide a massive boost to the defense. An ankle injury has kept him sidelined since the Broncos’ Week 5 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Hufanga already has 23 total tackles, three pass breakups, two interceptions (including a pick-six) and a forced fumble in just five games this season. More news : Aaron Rodgers Could Get 2 Key Weapons Back for Steelers-Eagles Showdown The timing couldn’t be better for Denver. The Broncos enter Week 11 with a 7-2 record and a five-game winning streak, sitting among the top teams in the AFC. They’ll host the 4-6 Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High, looking to extend their run to six straight wins and strengthen their position in the AFC West. Las Vegas is coming off two straight losses and will be looking to get back on track, making it an important opportunity for Denver to protect its position in the division. Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is still searching for his first win as Vegas’ starter. More news : Vikings Get Some Good News on Jordan Addison After Injury Scare More news : Nick Sirianni Makes Decision on Eagles OC Sean Mannion Amid Offensive Struggles Having five injured players back at practice is certainly encouraging, but none of them have been cleared for Sunday’s game. Waddle and Moss still have to complete the NFL ‘s concussion protocol before they can play, but the fact that they’re back at practice indicates that will probably happen in the next few days. Still, after a bye week that gave several players extra time to recover, the Broncos have plenty of reason to be optimistic heading into a crucial divisional clash. home.blurb: After a physical game against the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, the Raiders are dealing with a few bumps and bruises; nothing out of the ordinary. But the Broncos are coming off their bye, so they practically have a clean bill of health heading into this heated divisional matchup. Concussions can often keep a player out for one game, but because Denver had its bye week, both players were able to make a full recovery. And that's a good thing, because head and neck health is important, but it certainly does not help Las Vegas' chances of winning in Week 11. Matt Gay being a bit banged up is not great, either. He has been lights-out as a kicker this year, and with the ball moving differently at a mile above sea level on Sunday, Las Vegas needs him to be at the top of his game. Hip injuries can be worrisome for a kicker, depending on the hip, of course. With the Broncos not having any injury concerns this week, fresh off their bye, it hurts to have Bowers potentially out and another starter at least banged up. But the Raiders haven't done well playing against injured teams this year, so maybe they'll thrive with the shoe on the other foot. Not even close to everything has gone right for the Las Vegas Raiders during the 2026 NFL season. But one benefit that they've carried in their back pocket throughout the campaign has been relatively good health , which has given them an edge in seemingly every single game. Have the Silver and Black always taken advantage of that edge? No. But in several contests, they have gotten to face skeleton crews with a fully staffed roster. That is changing this week, though, with the AFC West rival Denver Broncos on the schedule for Week 11. All year, Las Vegas has been at an advantage in the injury department. Now, they're up against it. Broncos' injury report is as thin as it gets before clash with Raiders Both teams released their injury reports after Wednesday's practice. Here is how things went in Denver: Nobody is wishing injury on the Broncos, but of course, as fate would have it, they get a handful of key players back when they face the Raiders. Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss, both of whom suffered concussions in Week 9, are back at practice with no limitations and will play on Sunday. Talanoa Hufanga is also back this week, it seems, after missing four straight games for the Broncos' secondary. He was playing well before suffering an ankle injury, and he missed an entire month. But with an extra week off to prepare, he will re-emerge against the Raiders, of course. Caleb Loehner is also back this week after beginning the season on IR. He is a promising young tight end prospect that, if you can believe anything that Sean Payton says, has a bright future in Denver. The Broncos have been looking for a spark at tight end, so he could be involved right away. home.blurb: He’s the only member of the Raiders stung by multiple injuries. Plus became one of two who sat out this practice session, with defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway also sitting. Vegas is 4-6 overall and 0-1 since trading away week one starter Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. Cousins won in his Vikings return this past Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Las Vegas Raiders aim to see a rejuvenated Fernando Mendoza following his rough NFL debut. But he may need to roll without All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Bowers is dealing with ankle and quad injuries still. He didn’t participate in Wednesday practice according to the injury report . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Yet Bowers isn’t the only TE who landed on the injury report. Backup Ian Thomas is dealing with a calf ailment. Bowers played through pain against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, catching just two passes for 18 yards. Mendoza, again, received a rough welcome into the NFL. Seattle sacked him six times and bottled Mendoza to 143 yards . The Seahawks even sent star cornerback Devon Witherspoon on two blitzes, eventually leading to a team-high two sacks. Witherspoon even nailed Mendoza on a disguised overload blitz look that instead saw Seattle drop four defenders into coverage, but got Witherspoon busting freely down the middle. So the Raiders could see a thinner TE room. Michael Mayer is one healthy option the Silver and Black can turn to against Denver. home.headline: Broncos get boost regarding injuries days before facing Raiders
home.blurb: Coming out of their Week 10 bye, every player on the 53-man roster was present at Wednesday’s practice, including several key contributors who have been dealing with injuries. Related Articles NFL Calls Out NBC’s Mike Florio for On-Air Joke About Mike Vrabel The Denver Broncos could be getting some massive reinforcements at just the right time. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, cornerbacks Riley Moss and Kris Abrams-Draine, and safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones were all back on the field as Denver prepares for its AFC West showdown with the visiting Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Waddle and Moss are the biggest developments as both suffered concussions during Denver’s Week 9 win over the Carolina Panthers. Neither player finished that game, leaving the Broncos without two important pieces on opposite sides of the ball. Getting Waddle back would give quarterback Bo Nix another explosive receiving threat and Moss would help restore Denver’s starting cornerback pairing alongside Patrick Surtain II. Hufanga could also provide a massive boost to the defense. An ankle injury has kept him sidelined since the Broncos’ Week 5 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Hufanga already has 23 total tackles, three pass breakups, two interceptions (including a pick-six) and a forced fumble in just five games this season. More news : Aaron Rodgers Could Get 2 Key Weapons Back for Steelers-Eagles Showdown The timing couldn’t be better for Denver. The Broncos enter Week 11 with a 7-2 record and a five-game winning streak, sitting among the top teams in the AFC. They’ll host the 4-6 Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High, looking to extend their run to six straight wins and strengthen their position in the AFC West. Las Vegas is coming off two straight losses and will be looking to get back on track, making it an important opportunity for Denver to protect its position in the division. Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is still searching for his first win as Vegas’ starter. More news : Vikings Get Some Good News on Jordan Addison After Injury Scare More news : Nick Sirianni Makes Decision on Eagles OC Sean Mannion Amid Offensive Struggles Having five injured players back at practice is certainly encouraging, but none of them have been cleared for Sunday’s game. Waddle and Moss still have to complete the NFL ‘s concussion protocol before they can play, but the fact that they’re back at practice indicates that will probably happen in the next few days. Still, after a bye week that gave several players extra time to recover, the Broncos have plenty of reason to be optimistic heading into a crucial divisional clash. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. McCarthy, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the Jacksonville Jaguars, this is a big one. The Jaguars are set to face their toughest test since the bye week ended with the 5-3-1 New York Giants in Week 11. A game that head coach Liam Coen has already said will have to be won in the trenches will be a challenge the Jaguars haven't faced in Weeks. To preview the Jaguars and Giants clash as Jacksonville prepares for their second-half playoff run, we spoke with Patricia Traina of Giants OnSI to go behind the scenes and get an idea of what the Jaguars can really expect. So, how does Traina see this game from the Giants' perspective, and what will it take for Jacksonville to win? We break it down below. 1) What is Arvell Reese more dangerous at: playing linebacker or rushing the passer? Traina: Both. Overall, Reese ranks third among Giants linebackers (inside and outside) with 14 pressures per NFL+, and he has the second-lowest average time to sack (4.0 seconds) in that group. And the scary thing is that this young man, whose name has been mentioned for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors, is just getting started. Reese as a pass rusher (just 107 times so far) as he has been in coverage (246 times). I would think that as the game continues to slow down for him, he will see an increase in his role. 2) How do you view the matchup between Malik Nabers and Travis Hunter? Traina: I think that’s going to be a key matchup. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has done a good job of scheming Nabers open this season by moving him around the formation. When playing in the slot, he has an 84.6% reception rate and has scored both of his touchdowns from the slot. Travis Hunter hasn’t worked much from the slot this season. They have Hunter down as having played six total snaps in the slot, defending just one target that was not completed. I am very interested in seeing how much the Giants put Nabers in the slot on Sunday and, when he’s not in the slot, how much, if any, the Jaguars have Hunter travel with him. 3) How much have the Giants trusted J.J. McCarthy when it comes to attacking defenses downfield? Explosive plays have been one of the Jaguars’ few weaknesses. Traina: Overall, the Giants have a 44.7% passing completion rate (10th in the league) on deep balls of 20+ air yards. This season, McCarthy has a 52.6% completion rate on deep passes of 20+ air yards. As you might guess, Nabers has been the main target on those deep balls., he’s caught 12 of 21 (57.1%) with one drop. Rookie Malachi Fields has caught three of nine, and Darnell Mooney one of six. Tight end Isaiah Likely has caught three of seven deep passes. As I’m guessing the Jaguars will do everything possible to take Nabers out of the equation, I suspect this could be a good opportunity for Fields to have a breakout game. 4) What kind of impact has former Jaguars CB Greg Newsome made in New York? Traina: He’s been outstanding in coverage, so much so that the Giants recently gave him a three-year contract extension. He currently has a career-best 71.2 coverage grade from PFF and has allowed opponents just a 57.6% completion rate. Newsome has also allowed just 61 YAC, has yet to surrender a touchdown, and has five pass breakups, all good for a 63.8 NFL coverage rating, which is the best of his career. 5) If Jacksonville wins this game, what do you think would be the biggest reason why? They make the Giants one-dimensional. The Jaguars have one of the best run defenses in the league right now, and I’m fairly certain they’ll zero in on shutting down running back Cam Skattebo and challenging McCarthy to beat them through the air. McCarthy is 9-4 as a starter in games where his offense has rushed for 100+ yards collectively. That’s not to say McCarthy and the Giants can’t pull off the upset, but if they become one-dimensional, it’ll be that much harder for them to do so. As my readers and listeners have reminded me, the Giants ran up a storm against the Houston Texans a few weeks back, posting a season-high 188 yards against a Texans run defense that was top five going into that game. So yes, the Giants have a chance. Published 9 hours ago JOHN SHIPLEY John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. Q: Why has Trevor Lawrence been so surgical against zone coverage? Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. Liam Coen’s scheme also gives Lawrence and the passing game plenty of open looks against zone coverage, thanks to the balance they play with on offense and how they scheme open wide receivers. But most importantly, it comes down to how Lawrence is playing. He is confident in everything he is doing before and after the snap, far more confident than he has looked in past years. JS: When it comes to the Jaguars’ defense vs. the Giants’ offense, the biggest matchup I am going to be watching is Malik Nabers against Travis Hunter. Hunter has been a true shutdown No. 1 cornerback this season, even beyond his amazing athletic feats on his interceptions. He is the only Jaguars cornerback who can really run with Nabers, and I am fascinated to see these two battle downfield. The Jaguars don’t have their cornerbacks following receivers, but this might be the week to consider it. As for the Jaguars’ offense vs. the Giants’ defense, I am going with Walker Little against Abdul Carter. Little has played well for the Jaguars since stepping in as the starting left tackle a month ago due to injuries, but a player on Carter’s level hasn’t tested him. Little has proven he can get the job done week in and week out, but this week will be about proving that he can handle playing a blue-chip talent, which is exactly what he will need to do during a critical playoff run. Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

Q: The Jags have been blowing out opponents. What are your expectations for this week, though? The Giants have fought hard week in and week out under John Harbaugh, and I think there is a real chance they take the fight to the Jaguars in the trenches. We step behind enemy lines this week by checking in with Jacksonville Jaguars On SI site publisher John Shipley, who offers insight into the key matchups and intangibles to watch when the New York Giants host the Jaguars. Q: Why has Trevor Lawrence been so surgical against zone coverage? JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. Liam Coen’s scheme also gives Lawrence and the passing game plenty of open looks against zone coverage, thanks to the balance they play with on offense and how they scheme open wide receivers. But most importantly, it comes down to how Lawrence is playing. He is confident in everything he is doing before and after the snap, far more confident than he has looked in past years. He knows where the ball is going, and he knows how to fit it in there regardless of how open or tight the passing windows are. Q: How does the potential absence of center Robert Hainsey affect the offensive line? JS: It will likely impact communication. The Jaguars’ offense has had some communication issues on the road this year, whether in Denver in Week 2 or in London in Weeks 5-6. That said, this might not be the crushing loss many outside Jacksonville believe it is. Hainsey has been the Jaguars’ fifth-best offensive lineman this season, and a lot of his value comes pre-snap. There is a real chance the Jaguars could see stronger play from second-year center Jonah Monheim, whom the staff rates extremely highly and who has played well in spot starts for Hainsey in the past. away.headline: Jaguars-Titans Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Full-Go Status Puts Focus on Rushing Attack
away.blurb: The Jaguars are set to be without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III against the Titans as the Jaguars give them their bye week, while defensive end BJ Green will also be out as he works his way back from the injured reserve list. Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans. The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game. As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. But in an AFC where the race for the No. 1 seed will be important week in and week out, and the Jaguars will need their running game to continue hitting its stride over the second-half of the season. But Campanile has built one of the best run defenses in the NFL, and his philosophy of forcing quarterbacks to get the ball out of their hands quickly has led to plenty of takeaways and big plays. Q: The Jags have been blowing out opponents. What are your expectations for this week, though? The Giants have fought hard week in and week out under John Harbaugh, and I think there is a real chance they take the fight to the Jaguars in the trenches. We step behind enemy lines this week by checking in with Jacksonville Jaguars On SI site publisher John Shipley, who offers insight into the key matchups and intangibles to watch when the New York Giants host the Jaguars. Q: Why has Trevor Lawrence been so surgical against zone coverage? JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. Liam Coen’s scheme also gives Lawrence and the passing game plenty of open looks against zone coverage, thanks to the balance they play with on offense and how they scheme open wide receivers. But most importantly, it comes down to how Lawrence is playing. He is confident in everything he is doing before and after the snap, far more confident than he has looked in past years. He knows where the ball is going, and he knows how to fit it in there regardless of how open or tight the passing windows are. Q: How does the potential absence of center Robert Hainsey affect the offensive line? JS: It will likely impact communication. The Jaguars’ offense has had some communication issues on the road this year, whether in Denver in Week 2 or in London in Weeks 5-6. That said, this might not be the crushing loss many outside Jacksonville believe it is. Hainsey has been the Jaguars’ fifth-best offensive lineman this season, and a lot of his value comes pre-snap. There is a real chance the Jaguars could see stronger play from second-year center Jonah Monheim, whom the staff rates extremely highly and who has played well in spot starts for Hainsey in the past. He is the only Jaguars cornerback who can really run with Nabers, and I am fascinated to see these two battle downfield. home.headline: Giants Cam Skattebo Reveals Backflip Celebration's Future After Aidan Hutchinson's Knee Injury
home.blurb: Cam Skattebo is retiring the backflip. The New York Giants' running back said he will no longer do his signature celebration after seeing Detroit Lions' pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL during a sack celebration on Sunday. "It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Monday. "I'm saying yeah [no more backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me." He did add that he might bring back the backflip "if we go to the playoffs or something," but acknowledged that Hutchinson "didn't think about [the risk] either, and it happened." You have to think folks with the Giants' organization were jumping for joy—backflipping for joy, even—after hearing Skattebo's comments on the matter.
