LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for this week, and the Vikings have started as a three-point underdog to the Niners. The over/under for this one has started at 46.5 points. The Vikings snapped their two-game losing streak this past Sunday at Lambeau Field, pasting the Green Bay Packers by a score of 30-10 to complete a sweep of the Border Battle for the 2026 season. The defense was dominant, sacking Jordan Love eight times and forcing three of the four turnovers committed by the Packers (the fourth came on special teams). But the big story was the Vikings' offense and the return of Kirk Cousins, whom the Vikings acquired at the trade deadline on Tuesday, arrived in Minnesota on Wednesday, and started on Sunday, making him the first player since at least 1950 to start games at quarterback for different teams in consecutive weeks. Cousins' last start for his former team, the Las Vegas Raiders, came against these same 49ers, who come into this game tied for the league's best record at 8-1. Like the Vikings, the Niners got their season off to a 6-0 start before seeing their first loss, a 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. After the bye, they came back to beat Cousins and the Raiders by a score of 38-17, and this past Sunday they had a back-and-forth battle with the Dallas Cowboys that saw them eventually emerge with a 46-40 victory at Jerryworld. Brock Purdy is on the short list of potential MVP candidates for this season, and he showed why against the Cowboys, completing 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns, two of which came on long passes to Christian McCaffrey, who had 161 receiving yards on the day. This matchup looks to be another matchup of a very strong offense facing off against Brian Flores' #1 defensive squad. Unlike what we saw when the Vikings faced the Bills on Monday Night, however, now it appears that the Vikings have the offense to actually allow their defense to have a bit of a rest and not allow them to get worn down late in the game. For the fourth consecutive week, the Vikings will go into a game as an underdog, ladies and gentlemen. What do you think about that? Let us know in the comments!

away.blurb: Packers list seven questionable, rule out four vs. Vikings | Week 10 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News S Xavier McKinney (foot) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday Evan Siegle, packers.com S Xavier McKinney GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed seven players questionable and ruled out four for Sunday's NFC North showdown with the Minnesota Vikings at Lambeau Field. The seven questionable are safety Xavier McKinney (foot), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (back), safety Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps) and running back Chris Brooks (ankle). Running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee) have been ruled out. Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) has been listed as doubtful after not practicing this week. McKinney was added to the injury report Friday after being listed as limited in practice. He has not missed a game due to injury since 2022 with the New York Giants. Moore and Brooks are currently on injured reserve with a designation to return and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play Sunday. Moore got off to a fast start as Green Bay's primary kickoff and punt returner before injuring his ankle against Chicago last month. He's averaging 16.0 yards per punt return with a 27.5-yard average on kickoffs. Green Bay's starting nickel cornerback returned to practice Friday on a limited basis. He's played in 31 consecutive games for the Packers (including playoffs). Van Ness, who leads the Packers with 13 quarterback hits and 4½ sacks this season, played 32 snaps in Sunday's 45-27 win over New England but did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday before returning in a limited capacity. Kicker Trey Smack (right calf), linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper (illness), guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) and receiver Savion Williams (groin) didn't receive a game status and will be available Sunday. The Vikings have ruled out quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring), linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion), defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) and tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest). Outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy (calf), S Joshua Metellus (shoulder) and receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) are questionable. Minnesota didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: safety Jay Ward (knee), safety Theo Jackson (quad), tackle Christian Darrisaw (rest), safety Harrison Smith (rest) and quarterback Carson Wentz (ankle). ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window * The Vikings did not practice on Wednesday; the report is an estimation. news Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report CB Keisean Nixon, two running backs questionable for Sunday CB Keisean Nixon has been added to the injury report and is questionable for tonight's game

away.headline: Vikings-Packers Second Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. The suspension stems from a New Year’s Eve incident in which Nacua was accused of biting a woman at a dinner, according to Ari Meirov. The Rams and 49ers face each other on Dec. 13.
